name: Skyflow Forms – Simple & Multi-Step Form Builder for Contact Forms & Lead Generation
author: Seventh Sky

sections.description:
Skyflow WordPress Contact Form Builder includes the visual builder, essential input fields, submission storage, CSV export, admin email notifications, user confirmation emails, and a submissions analytics dashboard. Start with a simple contact form, then add fields and customize the layout as your needs change.

Need a multi-step form, conditional questions, file uploads, or calculated totals? These are available through the separate Skyflow Forms Pro add-on.

Create the forms your website needs

  • Contact and enquiry forms: Collect a visitor’s name, email address, phone number, and message.
  • Lead generation forms: Capture contact details and let visitors choose the service they are interested in.
  • Request a quote forms: Gather project details with text, dropdowns, and checkboxes. Add calculated estimates with Pro.
  • Feedback forms: Ask questions using radio buttons, dropdowns, and consent fields. Add ratings with Pro.
  • Signup and interest forms: Collect email addresses and preferences, with optional confirmation emails.
  • Multi-step forms with Pro: Split longer enquiries into pages with previous and next buttons and progress text.

Include an Email field in each form: the current submission system requires a valid email address to save a response.

A visual form builder without code

Add fields by clicking a field card or dragging it onto the canvas. Reorder fields with drag handles or move controls, select a field to edit its settings, and preview the result before publishing.

  • Build responsive layouts with one to six columns.
  • Arrange fields inside column containers.
  • Set field labels, placeholder text, required status, help text, and widths.
  • Customize the form title, description, footer note, and alignment.
  • Choose a background preset, solid color, or image with opacity controls.
  • Style the submit button’s text, color, size, appearance, and position.
  • Preview desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts.
  • Duplicate an existing form when you need a similar layout.
  • Enable or disable a saved form from the forms list.

Free contact form fields

The following fields are included in Skyflow Forms Core:

  • Name
  • Email
  • Simple Text
  • Text Area
  • Dropdown
  • Radio Field
  • Checkbox
  • Date
  • Consent
  • Phone
  • Submit Button

Phone fields can use a country calling-code selector or a plain phone input. Date fields support minimum, maximum, and default dates. Consent fields let you write your own acknowledgement text.

Publish inline forms or popup forms

Every saved form has its own shortcode. Copy the exact shortcode from Skyflow Forms > All Forms, then paste it into a Shortcode block on a page or post, or another area that supports WordPress shortcodes.

Choose inline display to show the form within your content. For a modal popup, select Modal Popup and use the form’s generated CSS trigger class on a link, button, or other element. Copy the class shown for that form instead of guessing its ID.

After submission, display a custom thank-you message, show a message before redirecting, or redirect immediately to a chosen URL.

Manage submissions in WordPress

Keep responses in your WordPress database and review them from Skyflow Forms > Submissions.

  • Filter by form, date range, and read status.
  • Search email addresses and stored field values.
  • Open a response to review its saved field data and submission details.
  • Mark responses as read or unread.
  • Move responses to Trash or delete them permanently.
  • Apply bulk actions to selected records.
  • Export submissions to CSV and choose which columns to include.

Repeat submissions: Records are associated with an email address and form. Submitting the same email address to the same form updates its existing record with the latest response, rather than creating a separate history entry for every submission.

Send notifications and confirmation emails

Configure email delivery under Skyflow Forms > Settings > Emails. Notify your team when someone submits a form and optionally send a confirmation to the visitor.

Customize recipients, subjects, message content, reply-to behavior, and supported email formatting. Personalize messages with merge tags such as:

  • {form_name}
  • {submission_id}
  • {submitted_at}
  • {email}
  • {all_fields}
  • {site_name}
  • {site_url}
  • {admin_email}
  • {field:Your Field Label}

Name-based tags {first_name} and {last_name} are also supported; their values depend on the submitted field labels.

Emails use WordPress’s wp_mail() function. You can use an SMTP plugin to configure your site’s mail transport. Delivery depends on your hosting, mail provider, and sender configuration; the settings page includes a test-email tool.

Review submission trends

The free analytics dashboard shows submission totals, read and unread activity, charts over time, and top-performing forms. Filter by date range or focus on a specific form to review its activity.

Pro adds form-view and conversion metrics, completion and partial-entry statistics, country reporting, and an hourly activity view. Country reporting requires a configured geolocation source; external geolocation is disabled by default.

Extend your forms with Skyflow Forms Pro

Skyflow Form core plugin is free with all the basic required fields for standard users, however, if user like to use the addtional advanced field, it can be upgraded to Skyflow Forms Pro. Pro add-on inclueds

Advanced inputs and uploads

  • Mask Input, Address Fields, Country List, and Numeric Field
  • Multiple Choice and Multi-select Dropdown
  • Website URL and Time & Date
  • Image Upload and File Upload with file-type, size, and count settings
  • Rating fields
  • Custom HTML

Conditional logic and calculations

  • Show, hide, require, or clear fields and layout blocks based on earlier answers.
  • Combine rules with all/any matching.
  • Build calculated values using formulas and other field values.
  • Add hidden fields for static values, supported dynamic defaults, current-user information, or query-string values.

Multi-step and structured layouts

  • Page Break fields with previous/next navigation and configurable progress text
  • Accordions and tabs with nested fields
  • Section dividers, paragraphs, spacers, and image blocks

Captcha and policy acknowledgements

  • Google reCAPTCHA and hCaptcha fields
  • Terms & Conditions and GDPR consent fields

Captcha requires keys from the selected provider. Consent fields provide controls for collecting acknowledgements; you supply the policy text and configure them for your own use.

Explore Skyflow Forms Pro.

Documentation and support

Visit the support forum for questions and troubleshooting. The Support page in the plugin also links to documentation and other help resources.

External services and data

Core stores form definitions and responses in your site’s WordPress database. Notifications use your configured WordPress mail system; your chosen mail host or SMTP service processes those emails.

The optional integrations below make external requests. Skyflow Forms Core does not contain its own vendor license-validation service; Pro licensing is handled by the separate add-on.

Google reCAPTCHA (optional, Pro field)

When enabled and configured the integration loads Google’s reCAPTCHA JavaScript in visitors’ browsers. The browser contacts Google to obtain a response token. Server-side verification sends that token, the configured secret key, and the visitor IP address to https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify to check the response. The integration supports reCAPTCHA v2 and v3.

Google Terms of Service | Google Privacy Policy

hCaptcha (optional, Pro field)

When enabled and configured, the integration loads hCaptcha’s JavaScript from https://js.hcaptcha.com/1/api.js. Server-side verification sends the response token, configured secret key, and visitor IP address to https://hcaptcha.com/siteverify.

hCaptcha Terms of Service | hCaptcha Privacy Policy

Country geolocation (optional, Pro add-on)

External country lookups are disabled by default. Selecting ip-api Pro and saving a provider API key under Settings > Analytics enables HTTPS requests to https://pro.ip-api.com/json/, sending a visitor IP address and the provider key to retrieve a country code. The add-on caches lookup results. The built-in integration does not use ip-api’s free HTTP endpoint. A developer can supply a different country source through the skyflow_forms_pro_geolocation_country_code filter.

ip-api service and terms | ip-api Pro account

Pro licensing and updates (separate add-on)

When the Pro add-on is installed, its licensing and update components contact https://7thskysoftware.com/ for activation, deactivation, license validation, and update checks. Requests can include the license key, site domain, product identifier, and installed version information, including WordPress version for update checks. This is separate from free Core functionality.

Vendor Privacy Policy | Vendor Terms of Service
sections.installation:
Install from your WordPress dashboard

  1. Open Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  2. Search for Skyflow Forms.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  4. Open Skyflow Forms > New Form.

Install a ZIP file

  1. Download the Skyflow Forms plugin ZIP.
  2. Open Plugins > Add New Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  3. Choose the ZIP, click Install Now, and activate the plugin.

Create and publish your first contact form

  1. Open Skyflow Forms > New Form and name your form.
  2. Add an Email field and any other fields you need. New forms start with a one-column container and a Submit button.
  3. Select fields to customize their labels, required status, and other settings.
  4. Preview the form and click Save Form.
  5. Open All Forms, copy its shortcode, and add it to a Shortcode block on your page.
  6. Configure notifications under Settings > Emails.
  7. Submit a test response and check both Submissions and your notification inbox.
sections.faq:
Is Skyflow Forms free?

Yes. Core includes the visual builder, basic fields, responsive column containers, inline and modal display, email notifications, stored submissions, CSV export, and submission analytics. Advanced fields and capabilities listed in the Pro section require the separate paid add-on and an active license.

Can I build forms without coding?

Yes. Add fields visually, arrange them in containers, edit their settings, and use the preview to check the result. Publish an inline form with its generated shortcode.

How do I embed a form in WordPress?

Copy the form’s exact shortcode from Skyflow Forms > All Forms and paste it into a Shortcode block. Themes and page builders can display it wherever they support WordPress shortcode output.

Does the free plugin support multi-column forms?

Yes. Containers with one to six columns are included in Core. Enable stacking on mobile when configuring a container, and check the mobile preview before publishing.

Are multi-step forms free?

No. Multi-step forms use the Pro Page Break field. Core includes responsive multi-column layouts; Pro adds page-by-page navigation and progress text.

Can I use conditional logic or calculate a quote?

Yes, with Pro. Conditional logic changes fields based on visitor answers. Calculation fields let you build formulas for values such as quantities or estimates. These features do not add payment processing.

Does a form need an email address?

Yes. The current submission handler requires a valid email address. Include an Email field even if the rest of your form mainly collects feedback or project information.

What happens when someone submits the same form again?

If the email address and form match an existing record, the plugin updates that record with the latest submission. It does not store each repeat submission as an independent entry.

Can visitors upload documents or images?

Yes, with Pro’s File Upload and Image Upload fields. Configure the allowed types, maximum size, and number of files for the field.

Where are responses saved, and can I export them?

Responses are saved in your WordPress database. Review them under Submissions and export CSV data if your role has export permission. The export settings let you choose columns.

Why am I not receiving notification emails?

Check that notifications are enabled and the recipient address is correct under Settings > Emails, then send a test email. Check spam folders and your site’s mail configuration. An SMTP plugin can help configure delivery through your mail provider.

Can I show a thank-you message or redirect after submission?

Yes. Choose a message only, a message followed by a delayed redirect, or an immediate redirect in the form’s settings.

Can I open a form from a button or link?

Yes. Choose Modal Popup display and apply the generated trigger class to your button or link. Use the class provided for that form in All Forms.

Is a vendor account required to use the free builder?

No. Core form building, local submission storage, and email notifications do not require a Skyflow vendor account or paid license. Pro activation and optional external providers have their own requirements.

Does Skyflow Forms integrate with a newsletter or CRM service?

Core saves contact details locally and exports CSV files. It does not include a built-in connection to a newsletter delivery or CRM service. A signup form does not by itself subscribe someone to an external mailing platform.

Is Google reCAPTCHA or hCaptcha included?

The captcha fields require Pro and provider keys configured under Settings > Security. These integrations use external services as described below.

Where are the License and geolocation settings?

With Pro installed, open Settings > License to manage the license and Settings > Analytics to configure country geolocation. Each tab requires its corresponding management permission.

What personal data can the plugin store?

Saved responses can include submitted field values, email address, source URL, IP address, browser user agent, and the WordPress user ID for logged-in visitors. Optional Pro uploads and analytics can store additional data. Review your forms, access permissions, and privacy notice for the information you collect.

Does the plugin provide an unsubscribe form?

Yes. Use [skyflow_unsubscribe] on a page and select that page under Settings > Unsubscribe. This changes the email address’s subscription status in Skyflow Forms’ local records, not in an external email service.
sections.changelog:
1.0.6 – 2026-11-22

  • Centered the Support page and added an official 7th Sky plugin-page card above the support resources.
  • Released the accumulated form-builder, Phone field, Upgrade page, and settings-navigation improvements from the 1.0.5 development series.
  • Updated the active plugin readme with revised feature descriptions, setup guidance, FAQs, and external-service disclosures.
  • Removed Tested up to from the PHP plugin header; compatibility metadata remains in the active readme.
  • Normalized country-helper line endings to resolve the mixed-line-endings warning.

1.0.5.9 – 2026-11-22

  • Renamed the Forms submenu label to All Forms.
  • Added responsive benefit cards and an accessible, horizontally scrollable feature comparison.
  • Fixed Phone field country-code selector sizing so it stays within frontend form columns.
  • Improved phone input flex behavior so the country code remains compact and the phone number uses the remaining width.
  • Added a country calling-code selector to Phone fields on the frontend and builder preview.
  • Added a Phone field setting for choosing between the country-code selector and a plain phone input.
  • Added responsive styling for phone country-code controls.

1.0.5

  • Updated WordPress compatibility metadata to tested up to 7.1.
  • Standardized builder and admin toggle controls for more consistent sizing and behavior, replacing remaining tick-style on/off settings with toggle switches where appropriate.
  • Added free Date and Consent field types to the Core builder, including frontend rendering, validation, saving, preview support, and submission/export display.
  • Added Core registry support and Pro-locked upsell cards for Calculation and Hidden Field Pro field types, with improved Pro detection so these fields remain disabled unless Skyflow Forms Pro is active.
  • Added role and capability access controls under Settings > Access, including custom permissions for managing forms, viewing submissions, exporting data, managing settings, and managing Pro licenses.
  • Updated Core admin menus, pages, POST handlers, AJAX handlers, and export actions to enforce the new Skyflow Forms-specific capabilities.
  • Hid export controls from users who can view submissions but do not have export permissions.
  • Improved role discovery to include registered roles, roles exposed through editable-role filters or stored role options, and custom role slugs discovered from user capability metadata.
  • Improved compatibility with custom role managers and roles created by membership, ecommerce, LMS, and other plugins, including capability syncing that registers discovered custom roles when needed.

1.0.4

  • Updated WordPress compatibility to 7.0.
  • Added Form Settings alignment controls for form title, description, and footer note.
  • Improved builder preview and frontend form consistency.
  • Added frontend and preview pagination behavior for Pro Page Break fields.
  • Fixed Section Divider frontend spacing and alignment output.
  • Fixed Address Fields option save/restore and frontend rendering for enabled address subfields.
  • Added core dispatch and validation support for Pro Multi-select Dropdown.

1.0.3

  • Builder canvas shows default field labels (e.g. Email, Phone) without opening Input Customization.
  • Fixed PHP 8.1+ deprecations when null reached merge tags and email handling.
  • Submissions CSV: optional column picker; exports include saved form field values.
  • Improved builder Form Settings labels and placeholders for clearer contact-form wording.
  • Added customizable Thank You Message after successful submissions.
  • Added post-submit redirect options: message only, message then redirect, or immediate redirect.
  • Fixed Input Customization sidebar textareas rendering too small in admin.
  • Improved builder drag-and-drop with handles and accurate insertion placeholder between top-level items.

1.0.2

  • Bug fixes and stability improvements.
  • Fixed form builder save and update staying on editor with success notices.
  • Fixed dropdown and radio options not saving inside layout containers.
  • Fixed form content not displaying on the frontend shortcode output.
  • Added preset, solid color, and image backgrounds with opacity controls.

1.0.1

  • Added drag-and-drop container layouts with 1–6 column support.
  • Added email notification system with admin alerts and user auto-responder.
  • Added global validation messages with token support.
  • Added analytics dashboard with KPI cards, charts, and date filtering.
  • Added live preview modal with desktop, tablet, and mobile switcher.
  • Added 5 new Pro fields: Terms & Conditions, GDPR Consent, reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Rating.
  • Added Accordion and Tabs layout blocks (Pro).
  • Redesigned Settings page with modern card-based UI.
  • Added Upgrade and Support admin pages.
  • Improved form builder stability, field reordering, and nested drag-and-drop.
  • Fixed frontend rendering issues for placeholders, labels, and container layouts.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
